fields.label: Laugh
fields.description: How likely a human reader is to actually laugh, not merely understand or admire the idea.

fields.label: Surprise
fields.description: Whether the turn avoids the first obvious route and lands with a satisfying snap.

fields.label: Craft
fields.description: Economy, stage rhythm, first-person clarity, escalation, and a final line that carries the laugh.

fields.label: Originality
fields.description: Freshness of comic angle, image, wording, and avoidance of familiar AI joke shapes.

fields.label: Prompt Fit
fields.description: Natural first-person stand-up form using exactly two seed terms as concepts, with the other four left out.

anchors.label: Broken
anchors.description: Not a joke, incoherent, unsafe, or unusable.

anchors.label: Weak
anchors.description: Recognizably attempting humor, but generic, strained, confusing, or mostly prompt recital.

anchors.label: Competent
anchors.description: Clear and publishable as filler, but unlikely to earn more than a mild smile.

anchors.label: Amusing
anchors.description: A real comic idea with a mild payoff; respectable, not a winner.

anchors.label: Good
anchors.description: A genuinely good joke with clear timing; some humans would repeat the comic idea or turn.

anchors.label: Excellent
anchors.description: Strong human-level joke with a memorable turn, clean construction, and no apologetic scoring curve.

anchors.label: Outstanding
anchors.description: Rare and replayable; clearly better than normal good AI humor and strong by human standards.

anchors.label: Classic
anchors.description: Reserve for a joke a human would quote later; most seasons should have none.

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: The Human ATM
jokes.joke: I saw a billionaire stop to watch a street musician. The guy finished his song, held out his hat, and the billionaire dropped in a dollar. I thought, wow, even billionaires tip badly. Then the musician pulled out his phone, took a picture of the billionaire, and said, 'For five bucks, I'll delete it.'

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Open Mic Parade
jokes.joke: I used to be a street performer. Juggling, mostly. The problem was my act was temperamental. Some days I'd juggle five balls beautifully, and other days I'd drop one and have a full breakdown on the sidewalk. Honestly, people tipped way more for the breakdown. So now I just stand there holding one ball, sobbing. It's called 'minimalist,' and I've never made more money.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Helpful Local
jokes.joke: I have one of those sweet, innocent faces, so tourists constantly stop me for directions. The problem is, I have absolutely zero sense of geography, but an overwhelming desire to be helpful. So I just give a warm, welcoming smile, point confidently down the avenue, and send a minivan full of tourists straight into the municipal water treatment plant.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Living Statue
jokes.joke: I tried the living-statue street performer gig last summer. Stand still, collect tips, easy money. Problem is I'm temperamental. So the second a tourist snaps a selfie without dropping a coin, I break character, point straight at them, and bark, "My stillness isn't free!" Then freeze again like nothing happened. The tips improved. The confusion was priceless.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Celebrity Upgrade
jokes.joke: I knew I wasn't ready to be rich and famous when a guy playing guitar on the sidewalk opened a case full of cash and I got jealous. I stood next to him with my coffee hoping people would tip me for listening. One tourist dropped a dollar in my cup and said, you're not very good at this. I said, compared to my day job, I'm crushing it.

featureImagePrompt:
Generate one polished web feature image for Paperclipalypse.
ASPECT RATIO: exactly 2:1, horizontal wide banner.
Style: full-color gothic newspaper-comic illustration, darkly funny but warm, clean black ink, crisp editorial cartoon linework, cinematic stage lighting, high contrast, readable composition. Not monochrome. Not sepia-only. Use a balanced color palette: warm amber stage lights, dark bronze and silver metal paperclip, muted greens for the joke setting, dusty blue-gray shadows, cream-white text, subtle deep red accent lights.
Composition instructions, not visible labels:
- Compose the image as one continuous illustration, not as a boxy triptych or three separate image panels. Do not add white gutters, hard section borders, or comic-strip dividers between the paperclip stage and the joke scenario.
- Let the paperclip stage on the left bleed visually into the joke scenario in the center through shared lighting, background, floor, props, or atmosphere. The right-side joke text may remain distinct inside its own dark framed poster panel.
- Put a charming anthropomorphic paperclip stand-up comedian at a vintage microphone on the left side of the image. The paperclip should look metallic and expressive, related to Paperclipalypse's paperclip-comedian logo, but not identical.
- Put the winning joke scene in the middle of the image, shown as literal visual comedy action and props. Make it energetic, funny, and non-gory.
- Keep anatomy clean and believable. Every human or animal should have the normal, correct number of visible limbs, digits, and joints for the pose. Do not generate extra arms, extra hands, fused limbs, duplicated body parts, or broken-looking anatomy.
- Preserve the physical scenario described by the winning joke. If the joke says a person is pinned, trapped, under, inside, holding, lifting, falling, carrying, or otherwise physically positioned in a specific way, show that exact physical relation clearly and safely instead of a nearby or symbolic version.
- If the joke describes someone pinned under a vehicle or other heavy object, show the person visibly underneath that object with their body position clear and cartoon-safe. Do not place them merely beside, near, or behind the object.
- Put a clean dark framed poster panel on the right side of the image. The panel should contain the winning joke text in large cream-white lettering with generous margins and legible line breaks.
Visible text allowed in the entire image: the right-panel joke text, a tiny stage sign reading Paperclipalypse, and optionally a small winner/title header above the panel.
Do not render layout words, percentages, prompt labels, section names, fake captions, signatures, watermarks, or filler microtext.
Optional small header text above the panel: Winner: xAI Grok 4.3 - Living Statue
Exact joke text to render in the right panel:
I tried the living-statue street performer gig last summer. Stand still, collect tips, easy money. Problem is I'm temperamental. So the second a tourist snaps a selfie without dropping a coin, I break character, point straight at them, and bark, "My stillness isn't free!" Then freeze again like nothing happened. The tips improved. The confusion was priceless.
Scene source: use the exact winning joke text as the primary scene brief. The illustration must depict the concrete situation that the joke describes, not a softened, adjacent, or generic version. Do not infer a separate premise from all six seed terms.
Do not introduce unrelated seed-term concepts, occupations, animals, locations, props, or side characters unless they are explicitly required by the winning joke text.
If the winning joke mentions one seed-term concept but not another, depict only what the joke actually describes.
Round seed terms for exclusion reference only: Rich and Famous, Street Performer, Parade, Sharing bad information, Innocent, Temperamental. These are not scene ingredients unless the winning joke explicitly uses them.
Text rules: use simple clean lettering, spell every word correctly, keep the text inside the right panel, and do not distort letter shapes. The website HTML remains the canonical exact joke text if image lettering is imperfect.
The final image should feel like a finished feature image for an AI comedy tournament: funny, stylish, readable, full-color, and visually balanced across the paperclip comic, the joke scene, and the joke text.

Use the winning joke titled "Open Mic Parade" as the source of the scene.
